items.value: A sabotaged publicity stunt sees a successful businesswoman fall to her death during a Cinco de Mayo parade.

On Monday afternoon, the city's Cinco de Mayo celebrations ended in tragedy when one of the parade's publicity stunts went horrifically wrong, resulting in the death of Lula Miguel (42), co-founder of the event's key sponsor Avos4all. This was the first year that Lula's avocado-producing business had won the lucrative contract to sponsor and supply the city's famous celebrations, which is believed to see several million dollars' worth of the fruit (yes, avocados are fruit!) consumed every year on this one day alone. To mark the occasion, Avos4all had arranged for a giant avocado-shaped hot air balloon to float over the parade. It's been reported that from the balloon, a number of golden avocados were floated down by parachute into the crowd. The lucky few to catch them were awarded with a lifetime supply of avocados. The euphoria generated by the golden avocado drop was, however, short-lived. Moments later, parade-goers were left stunned when they witnessed four skydivers jump from the sponsor's balloon, of which only three safely deployed parachutes; the fourth was left to plummet to the ground in front of many horrified eyewitnesses! At this point in time, the only statement made by the police has been to confirm the identity of the victim. No further comment has been made on the incident, which suggests they consider it more than just an avocado-themed marketing stunt gone wrong! Sandra Feldman, Crime Reporter & Co-host of the Murderous Mysteries podcast.

Summary of Incident: Four senior employees of Avos4all planned to parachute from the corporate hot air balloon at 1 p.m. during the Cinco de Mayo parade. The balloon launched an hour before this from the company's private airfield on the outskirts of town. At 9 a.m. that day, several of the jumpers carried out a safety check of their skydive equipment together at the airfield, including packing their own parachutes. They subsequently stored the equipment in one of the premises' private, pin code locked safety storage rooms, to which only the four Avos4all employees jumping that day were given the pin. The air balloon took flight shortly after 12 p.m., and it floated above the parade at an altitude of 3000ft for an hour prior to them jumping just after 1 p.m. An expert assessment of the faulty parachute confirms that it had been tampered with prior to launch, which caused it to fail, and resulted in the victim's death. Discovery: The victim's body was found immediately by attendees of the parade who watched the incident occur in real time. Time of Death: Just after 1 p.m. on Monday, May 5. Confirmed by multiple eyewitnesses. Evidence Collected: - The victim's parachute had been sabotaged with expertise. A specialist's opinion is that the sabotage could only have been carried out by a person with a detailed knowledge of, and experience in, handling parachutes. - Forensics discovered fresh fingerprints of all four jumpers on the entry pin pad to the storage room where the parachutes were being kept. - The entry pin pad kept a time log of its use. That morning it was used at 9 a.m., 11:15 a.m. and 11:50 a.m. Further Details: The victim's three colleagues, who were the only other people to have access to the storage room where the parachutes were kept, have been brought in for questioning.

Q: What was your relationship with Lula Miguel? A: We co-owned Avos4all so technically we were colleagues, but first and foremost she was my best friend. This Cinco celebration was a big deal for us - our first year as the main sponsor, a true sign of success in these parts! But not only that, it was in our home city, which made it extra special. Q: We understand there were rumors of Lula planning to leave Avos4all, is there any truth to these? A: Sadly yes, she hit me with that curve ball a few weeks ago. Apparently now that the business was a success she was getting bored and wanted a new challenge. On a personal level I was disappointed as she's my friend and I liked us working together, but from a business perspective it was an issue. Most of our major clients came through her and it created uncertainty as to whether they would stick around if she left to start another business. Q: Whose idea was it to skydive from an avocado-shaped hot air balloon? A: It was my idea. I wanted our corporate sponsorship to be memorable, so I came up with the idea of the themed balloon and golden avocado drop. We needed to make a statement! The skydive was a last-minute inclusion - I decided that the occasion needed to be special for us too. Both Lula and I were keen skydivers, so jumping off the balloon down into the parade seemed like an awesome idea. Q: Who were the other people you jumped with? A: Other than me and Lula, there was Joseph, our Head of Marketing, and then there was my brother Russell who also works for us. Q: Please talk us through what you did that day leading up to the jump? A: I arranged for those of us jumping to meet at 9 a.m. to carry out safety checks on our equipment, standard protocol prior to a jump. Everyone was there apart from Russell who stayed in bed and didn't bother showing up until later. Sadly it was typical behavior for him - he has no excuse as he only lives 10 minutes away. Q: Why did you arrange the safety check at 9 a.m. when the launch wasn't due until 12 p.m.? A: Lula and I were due at a corporate breakfast with some important clients between 9:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. and couldn't afford to miss it as they were important guests of ours that day. It ran a little over, but we were still out on time to collect our equipment from the store at the same time as the others. The jump itself was planned for 1 p.m., which with a 12 p.m. launch gave us plenty of time to drop the golden avocados and watch the crowd's reactions.

Q: How was your relationship with Lula? A: I knew her well. She was my sister Gwen's best friend, and had been close with my family for years, even before they set up Avos4all together. Lula and I never got on though. She always looked down at me. She thought that because I didn't go to college or have big career aspirations that I was a waste of space and a drain on my family. So as you can imagine she got pissed when my sister recently gave me a well-paid job at Avos4all. Q: Why do you think Lula was pissed about that? A: Oh it was clear, on my first day she pulled me to one side and explained in no uncertain terms that I had no right being there. She told me that my sister Gwen felt the same and that they had only given me the job as an act of charity because my parents had pressured them… The thing is, I didn't mind that at all. As far as I'm concerned my sister 'Golden Gwen' as my family call her, was no better than me. She was just lucky to be Lula's friend. Lula was the one who actually ran the business and made it a success. As co-owner Gwen was just riding her wave, and to this day I can't understand how other people don't see that. Q: How did you become involved in the skydive that day? A: The jump was one of Gwen's wacky, spur of the moment ideas. She thought it would look great for the business if its owners were seen to do something fun and crazy during the parade. She asked me to join because we've done loads of jumps together over the years, and I think she just needed to make up the numbers. Q: Talk us through what you did that day leading up to the jump? A: Gwen sent everyone the pin code to the equipment storage room and asked us to come in at 9 a.m. to safety check our equipment. But I was feeling a bit rough from a late one the night before and didn't bother with that. I was home alone and took the opportunity to stay in bed and enjoy a lie in, a much better use of my time. I got to the balloon just as it was due to launch at 12 p.m. Q: So when did you collect your equipment from the store room? A: I never went to the store room, I messaged Gwen asking her to bring it to the balloon launch for me, I then did my own checks when we were on the balloon and waiting to jump. Don't worry I may not be a successful entrepreneur like my sister, but I wouldn't have jumped 3000ft if I thought it was unsafe. Q: Did anything of note happen after the balloon took to the sky? A: Yes, Lula died in a dramatic and awful way, witnessed by thousands of people! And now you're trying to find out who did it by questioning me, such a waste of time!

Q: What was your relationship with Lula? A: She employed me as her Head of Finance. She was a talented businesswoman who I admired, which is why I decided to switch allegiances and join Avos4all from a rival firm a few months ago. But I regretted it as soon as I got there. The amount of corruption and illegal activity going on was uncomfortable for me. I told Lula of my intentions to leave soon after arrival but she was enforcing a clause in my contract to see out the year. I wasn't happy about it, but some of the things she had exposed me to meant my professionalism had already been compromised, and she held that over me. Q: How did you become involved in the skydive that day? A: Gwen was super keen for senior members of the business to be involved in the stunt. Apparently it was good for the brand's image, made us more personable or something, anyway as the new Head of Finance she insisted I take part. I tried to use the excuse of not knowing how, but she got round that by arranging for a qualified instructor called Chris to do a tandem jump with me on the day. Honestly the experience was awful, I hate heights, so going up in the balloon an hour before we even jumped was like torture, I was terrified the whole time. Q: Talk us through what you did that day leading up to the jump? A: Gwen wanted us there at 9 a.m. to check the equipment, which was annoyingly early and a bit pointless for me as I had no idea what I was meant to be doing. The tandem instructor Chris arrived and did all the safety checks for our kit. As the balloon wasn't due to launch until 12 p.m. I had time to kill, so I persuaded Chris to go into the city center with me to get a decent breakfast. We got back at around 11:50 a.m. just in time to meet Gwen and Lula collecting the equipment before takeoff. I'd hoped going into town would help take my mind off the idea of falling 3000ft later that day, but unsurprisingly, Chris being a skydiving instructor, meant that all he wanted to talk about was skydiving! Q: Do you know of any reason why someone might have wanted to harm Lula? A: Not many people know this but Lula had decided to leave Avos4all, and from what I could tell Gwen wasn't happy about it. Probably because Lula was the brains of the outfit and she realized that she would be exposed when she left. Why do you ask? Was it not an accident?

Key Evidence
- The Police Report teaches us two important things about the killer. Firstly, they had knowledge and experience in handling parachutes. Secondly, their opportunity to tamper with the victim's parachute was at 11:15 a.m. The only other times the store room's pin pad shows use was at 9 a.m. when the equipment was initially stored after safety checks, and then again when it was subsequently collected at 11:50 a.m. right before the balloon's launch. At both these times we know from Gwen and Joseph's accounts that there were multiple people present. - Considering this knowledge we can rule Joseph out as a suspect. Not only had he never skydived before and therefore lacked the necessary knowledge, but he also had an alibi for 11:15 a.m., as he was in the city having breakfast with his tandem jump instructor, Chris. - Gwen was a vastly experienced and keen skydiver. She would have the ability to tamper with a parachute in the manner carried out in this crime. However, she could not have done it as she was entertaining clients at a corporate breakfast between 9:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. - Russell by his own admission is an experienced skydiver, so has the knowledge and ability to tamper with a parachute. He tells us that he was at home alone in bed all morning. Considering he lives only 10 minutes away from the crime scene, and his whereabouts cannot be verified, he also had the opportunity to carry out the sabotage at 11:15 a.m. - Russell claims to have not been to the store room where the parachutes were kept that morning, however we know from the police report that his fresh fingerprints were on the pin pad. He lied about having been in there.

Confession
I slept in that morning knowing I would miss the 9 a.m. safety check. In my mind it was too early, and I had plenty of time to do it later in the morning. Despite this, when I woke I had nasty messages from both Lula and Gwen. They were annoyed that I hadn't shown up and went off on one calling me disrespectful, a liability, and an embarrassment to the family name! It wasn't unusual for them to get frustrated at me, but I was so fed up with Lula treating me like that, and of my sister thinking she was superior to me. So I decided to do something about it. I eventually went in around 11 a.m. to check my equipment. No one saw me when I arrived, and I was the only person in the store room. That's when I decided my revenge would be to tamper with a parachute. I only did one as I thought doing two would look less like an accident and attract too much attention. However, by choosing to do Lula's parachute I was able to get revenge on my sister at the same time as I knew that without Lula, the business would be sure to fail, meaning everyone would be able to see for themselves that there is nothing special about 'Golden Gwen'.
